For the Petitioner : Mr. Sidharth Sudhanshu, Advocate For the State : Mr. Someshwar Roy, A.P.P.

For the O.P. No.2 : Mr. Rahul Dev, Advocate.
.....
Order No.08/ Dated:20.02.2023 Heard learned counsel for the parties.

Apprehending his arrest in connection with Topchanchi P.S. Case No. 29 of 2022 instituted under Sections 323, 498A, 504, 506, 34 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, the petitioner has moved to this Court for grant of privilege of anticipatory bail.
As per F.I.R., marriage between the parties was solemnized in the year 2016.

Allegation against the petitioner along with his family members is that after solemnization of marriage, they demanded Rs.
1 lakh cash and motorcycle as additional dowry.
Due to non-fulfilment of which, she was brutally assaulted and tortured and was threatened to kill her and ousted her from her matrimonial house.
It is further alleged that the petitioner used to visit her parental home and used to threaten of dire consequences.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that petitioner is innocent and has committed no offence at all rather he has been falsely implicated in this case.

It is further submitted that petitioner is willing to keep his wife with full honour and dignity and also filed petition under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act vide original suit no. 815 of 2021 which is still pending.
The matter was also resolved at Mahila Police Station but it did not yield any fruitful result.
Thereafter, general and omnibus allegation have been attributed against the petitioner.

It is lastly submitted that the petitioner undertakes to co-operate with the investigation of the case and also abide by all terms and conditions which may be imposed in the matter of granting anticipatory bail to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner may be extended the privilege of anticipatory bail.

Learned Addl.P.P appearing for the State assisted by learned counsel for the informant opposes the Bangali Kalindi @ Bangali Kalindi @ ... vs The State Of Jharkhand on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44778598/
1 prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioner and submitted that petitioner is husband and due to his fault the informant has been compelled to live life under destitution.

sentences.text: Maintenance case is also pending and no order has been passed yet.
Hence, petitioner does not deserve anticipatory bail.
Considering the facts and circumstances of this case, the nature of allegation coupled with materials on record
, I am inclined to grant privilege of anticipatory bail to the petitioner.

Accordingly, the petitioner is directed to surrender in the Court below within four weeks from today and in the event of his arrest or surrendering, he will be enlarged on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.20,000/-
(Rupees Twenty Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Dhanbad in connection with Topchanchi P.S. Case No. 29 of 2022 with the condition that he will co-operate with the investigation of the case and appear before the investigating officer as and when noticed by him and furnish his mobile number and photocopy of the Aadhar Card with an undertaking that he will not change his mobile number during the pendency of the case and subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

(Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, J.) R.K/
